translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianshou, on the day when Investigating Censor-in-Chief Zong Qinke performed his obeisance, thunder pealed though there were no clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of Tianshou (690), on the day Investigating Censor-in-Chief Zong Qinke made his bow of obeisance, thunder crashed though the sky was cloudless.

sentences.zh: 近鼓妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates drum omens.
translations.idiomatic: This too approximates a drum omen.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年六月丙寅，天晦，街鼓不鳴。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin of the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan, the sky was dim; the street drums did not sound.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingyin of the sixth month of the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (797), the sky turned murky and the street drums failed to sound.

sentences.zh: 中和二年十月，西北方無雲而雷。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhonghe, in the northwest there was thunder though no clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year of Zhonghe (882), thunder rolled in the northwest though no clouds were in sight.

sentences.zh: 天復三年十月甲午，有大聲出于宣武節度使廳事。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu, a great sound issued from the hall of the Xuanwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu of the tenth month of the third year of Tianfu (903), a tremendous noise burst forth from the hall of the Xuanwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 近鼓妖也。

translations.literal: This approximates drum omens.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates a drum omen.

sentences.zh: 魚孽如意中，濟源路敬淳家水碾柱將壞，易之為薪，中有鮎魚長尺餘，猶生。

translations.literal: Fish calamities. During the RuYi period, at the home of Lu Jingchun of Jiyuan, a water-mill pillar was about to break; when it was replaced with firewood, inside was a catfish more than a foot long, still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Fish calamities. During the Ruyi reign (692), at the home of Lu Jingchun in Jiyuan, a pillar of the household water mill was about to fail. When it was taken down for firewood, a catfish more than a foot long was found inside, still living.

sentences.zh: 近魚孽也。

translations.literal: This approximates fish calamities.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates a fish calamity.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，安南都護府江中有大蛇，首尾橫出兩岸，經日而腐，寸寸自斷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, in the river of the Protectorate General of Annan there was a great serpent whose head and tail stretched across both banks; after a day it rotted, inch by inch breaking apart of itself.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan (716), a great serpent appeared in the river at the Protectorate General of Annan, its head and tail spanning both banks. After a day it rotted away, severing itself inch by inch.

sentences.zh: 數日，江魚盡死，蔽江而下，十十五五相附著，江水臭。

translations.literal: Within days, all the fish in the river died, covering the river as they drifted downstream, clinging to one another in tens and fives; the river water stank.
translations.idiomatic: Within days every fish in the river died and drifted downstream in vast shoals, clustering ten and five together until the water reeked.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，渭水有蝦蟆大如鼎，里人聚觀，數日而失。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong period, in the Wei River there was a toad as large as a ding; villagers gathered to watch, and after several days it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era (705–707), a toad as large as a cauldron appeared in the Wei River. Villagers thronged to gaze at it; after several days it disappeared.

sentences.zh: 是歲大水。

translations.literal: That year there was a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: That same year brought catastrophic flooding.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年二月，晝，有魚長尺餘，墜於鄆州市，良久乃死。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe, during daytime, there was a fish more than a chi in length that fell into the market of Yan Prefecture city; after a long while it died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yuanhe 14 (819), in broad daylight a fish more than a foot long fell into the marketplace at Yuncheng in Yanzhou and died only after a long while.

sentences.zh: 魚失水而墜于市，敗滅象也。

translations.literal: A fish losing water and falling into the market is the image of defeat and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: A fish deprived of water falling into a marketplace portends defeat and ruin.

sentences.zh: 開成二年三月壬申，有大魚長六丈，自海入淮，至濠州招義，民殺之。

translations.literal: On the day renshen of the third month of the second year of Kaicheng, there was a great fish six zhang in length that entered the Huai from the sea; reaching Zhaoyi in Hao Prefecture, the people killed it.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the third month of Kaicheng 2 (837), a fish six zhang long came from the sea into the Huai, reached Zhaoyi in Haozhou, and the people killed it.

sentences.zh: 近魚孽也。

translations.literal: Nearly a fish calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a fish calamity.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，汜水河魚逆流而上，至垣曲、平陸界。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, fish in the Sishui River swam upstream, reaching the border of Yuanqu and Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 6 (879), fish in the Sishui River swam upstream as far as the border of Yuanqu and Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 魚，民象，逆流而上，民不從君令也。

translations.literal: Fish are the image of the people; swimming upstream means the people do not follow the ruler's commands.
translations.idiomatic: Fish symbolize the common people; when they swim against the current, the people are refusing to obey the ruler's orders.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，揚州雨魚。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi, fish rained down at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 2 (886), fish rained from the sky over Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 占如元和十四年。

translations.literal: Prognostication as in the fourteenth year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication accords with that for Yuanhe 14 (819).

sentences.zh: 蝗武德六年，夏州蝗。

translations.literal: Locusts. In the sixth year of Wude, locusts at Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts. In the sixth year of Wude (623), locusts struck Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蝗之殘民，若無功而祿者然，皆貪撓之所生。

translations.literal: How locusts harm the people is like those who receive salaries without merit—all are produced by greedy grasping.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravage the people as officeholders draw pay without merit; both spring from greedy, corrupt conduct.

sentences.zh: 先儒以為人主失禮煩苛則旱，魚螺變為蟲蝗，故以屬魚孽。

translations.literal: Earlier ru believed that when the ruler loses ritual propriety and government is vexing and harsh, then drought follows and fish and snails transform into insects and locusts; therefore they classify this under fish calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that when rulers abandon ritual and rule becomes vexing and harsh, drought ensues and fish and snails turn into locusts—hence locust plagues belong under fish calamity.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年六月，京畿旱蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Zhenguan, the capital region suffered drought and locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenguan 2 (628), drought and locusts struck the capital region.

sentences.zh: 太宗在苑中掇蝗祝之曰：「人以穀為命，百姓有過，在予一人，但當蝕我，無害百姓。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong in the park picked up locusts and prayed to them, saying: "People take grain as their life. If the common people have fault, it lies in me alone. Let them devour only me—do not harm the common people."
translations.idiomatic: In the imperial park Emperor Taizong picked up locusts and addressed them: "Grain is the life of the people. If the common people have sinned, the fault is mine alone. Devour only me—do not harm the people."

sentences.zh: 將吞之，侍臣懼帝致疾，遂以為諫。

translations.literal: When he was about to swallow them, attendants feared the emperor would fall ill and remonstrated accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to swallow them, his attendants feared he would fall ill and urgently remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「所冀移災朕躬，何疾之避？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What I hope is to shift the calamity upon my person—why avoid illness?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I mean to take the calamity upon myself. Why should I fear illness?"

sentences.zh: 遂吞之。

translations.literal: He then swallowed them.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed them.

sentences.zh: 是歲，蝗不為災。

translations.literal: That year locusts did not become a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: That year the locusts did no harm.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，徐州蝗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, locusts at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year of Zhenguan (629), locusts struck Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，德、戴、廓等州蝗。

translations.literal: In autumn, locusts in the prefectures of De, Dai, Kuo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn locusts afflicted De, Dai, Kuo, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，觀、兗、遼等州蝗。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fourth year, locusts in Guan, Yan, Liao, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year of Zhenguan (630), locusts struck Guan, Yan, Liao, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十一年秋，渠、泉二州蝗。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twenty-first year, locusts in the two prefectures of Qu and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-first year of Zhenguan (647), locusts struck Qu and Quan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，夔、絳、雍、同等州蝗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, locusts in the prefectures of Kui, Jiang, Yong, Tong, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 (650), locusts struck Kui, Jiang, Yong, Tong, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年三月，京畿蝗，無麥苗。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongchun, locusts in the capital region; no wheat seedlings remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongchun 1 (682), locusts devoured the capital region until not a wheat seedling was left.

sentences.zh: 六月，雍、岐、隴等州蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, locusts in Yong, Qi, Long, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, Yong, Qi, Long, and other prefectures suffered locusts.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，台、建等州蝗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou, locusts in Tai, Jian, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Changshou 2 (693), locusts struck Tai, Jian, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開元三年七月，河南、河北蝗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Kaiyuan, locusts in Henan and Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 3 (715), locusts ravaged Henan and Hebei.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，山東蝗，蝕稼，聲如風雨。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year, locusts in Shandong; they ate the crops, their sound like wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year of Kaiyuan (716), locusts in Shandong devoured the crops, their sound roaring like wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，貝州蝗，有白鳥數千萬，羣飛食之，一夕而盡，禾稼不傷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, locusts at Bei Prefecture; there were tens of millions of white birds that flew in flocks to eat them; in one night they were entirely gone, and the grain crops were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan (737), locusts infested Beizhou; tens of millions of white birds flew in flock to devour them, and in a single night the locusts vanished while the grain stood untouched.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年秋，蝗，關輔尤甚，米斗千錢。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Guangde, locusts, especially severe in the Guanfu region; grain a dou for a thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guangde 2 (764), locusts swept the empire, worst in the capital region, where grain sold for a thousand cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 興元元年秋，螟蝗自山而東際于海，晦天蔽野，草木葉皆盡。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xingyuan, caterpillar-locusts from the mountains eastward reached the sea, darkening heaven and covering the wilds; leaves of grass and trees were entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Xingyuan 1 (784), caterpillars and locusts spread from the mountains eastward to the sea, darkening the sky and blanketing the land until every leaf was stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年夏，蝗，東自海，西盡河、隴，羣飛蔽天，旬日不息，所至草木葉及畜毛靡有孑遺，餓殣枕道，民蒸蝗，曝，颺去翅足而食之。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Zhenyuan, locusts from the east at the sea westward to the end of the He and Long circuits; flying in flocks they covered the sky for ten days without ceasing; where they reached, leaves of grass and trees and the hair of livestock were without a single survivor; the starved lined the roads as pillows; the people steamed locusts, dried them in the sun, shook off wings and legs, and ate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenyuan 1 (785), locusts ranged from the eastern sea westward through the He and Long circuits; swarms blotted out the sky for ten days on end; wherever they passed, not a leaf or tuft of livestock hair remained; corpses of the starved lined the roads; people steamed locusts, sun-dried them, shook off the wings and legs, and ate them.

sentences.zh: 永貞元年秋，陳州蝗。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Yongzhen, locusts at Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Yongzhen 1 (805), locusts struck Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 元和元年夏，鎮、冀等州蝗。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Yuanhe, locusts in Zhen, Ji, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yuanhe 1 (806), locusts afflicted Zhen, Ji, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年秋，洪州螟蝗害稼八萬頃。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year of Changqing, caterpillar-locusts at Hong Prefecture harmed crops across eighty thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Changqing 3 (823), caterpillars and locusts at Hongzhou destroyed crops across eighty thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 開成元年夏，鎮州、河中蝗，害稼。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Kaicheng, locusts at Zhen Prefecture and Hezhong Circuit; crops harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaicheng 1 (836), locusts at Zhenzhou and Hezhong Circuit ravaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 二年六月，魏博、昭義、淄青、滄州、兗海、河南蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, locusts in Weibo, Zhaoyi, Ziqing, Cang Prefecture, Yanhai, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kaicheng 2 (837), locusts struck Weibo, Zhaoyi, Ziqing, Cangzhou, Yanhai, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，河南、河北鎮定等州蝗，草木葉皆盡。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year, locusts in Henan, Hebei, Zhending, and other prefectures; leaves of grass and trees were entirely gone.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaicheng 3 (838), locusts in Henan, Hebei, Zhending, and other prefectures stripped every leaf from grass and trees.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，幽、魏、博、鄆、曹、濮、滄、齊、德、淄、青、兗、海、河陽、淮南、虢、陳、許、汝等州螟蝗害稼。

translations.literal: In summer of the fifth year, caterpillar-locusts harmed crops in You, Wei, Bo, Yun, Cao, Pu, Cang, Qi, De, Zi, Qing, Yan, Hai, Heyang, Huainan, Guo, Chen, Xu, Ru, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaicheng 5 (840), caterpillars and locusts damaged crops across You, Wei, Bo, Yun, Cao, Pu, Cang, Qi, De, Zi, Qing, Yan, Hai, Heyang, Huainan, Guo, Chen, Xu, Ru, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國多邪人，朝無忠臣，居位食祿，如蟲與民爭食，故比年蟲蝗。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The state has many evil men; the court has no loyal ministers; those in office eating salaries are like insects competing with the people for food—therefore year after year insect locusts."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "When the state teems with wicked men and the court lacks loyal ministers, officeholders who draw salaries are like insects competing with the people for food—hence insects and locusts year after year."

sentences.zh: 會昌元年七月，關東、山南鄧唐等州蝗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Huichang, locusts in Guandong, Shannan's Deng, Tang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Huichang 1 (841), locusts struck Guandong and the Deng, Tang, and other prefectures of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 大中八年七月，劍南東川蝗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Dazhong, locusts in Jiannan's Dongchuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Dazhong 8 (854), locusts infested Dongchuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年六月，淮南、河南蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Xiantong, locusts in Huainan and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiantong 3 (862), locusts ravaged Huainan and Henan.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，東都、同華陝虢等州蝗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the sixth year, locusts in the Eastern Capital, Tong, Hua, Shan, Guo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xiantong 6 (865), locusts afflicted the Eastern Capital and Tong, Hua, Shan, Guo, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 七年夏，東都、同、華、陝、虢及京畿蝗。

translations.literal: In summer of the seventh year, locusts in the Eastern Capital, Tong, Hua, Shan, Guo, and the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xiantong 7 (866), locusts struck the Eastern Capital, Tong, Hua, Shan, Guo, and the capital region.

sentences.zh: 九年，江淮、關內及東都蝗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, locusts in the Jiang-Huai region, Guannei, and the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 9 (868), locusts ravaged the Jiang-Huai, Guannei, and the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，陝、虢等州蝗。

translations.literal: In summer of the tenth year, locusts in Shan, Guo, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Xiantong 10 (869), locusts struck Shan, Guo, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 不絀無德，虐取於民之罰。

translations.literal: Failing to dismiss those lacking in virtue—the punishment for cruel seizure from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Failing to purge the unworthy is the penalty exacted when rulers cruelly strip the people.

sentences.zh: 乾符二年，蝗自東而西蔽天。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfu, locusts from east to west veiled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 2 (875), locusts spread from east to west until they blotted out the heavens.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年秋，蝗，自東方來，羣飛蔽天。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Guangqi, locusts came from the east; flying in flocks they veiled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Guangqi 1 (887), locusts arrived from the east in swarms that blotted out the sky.

sentences.zh: 二年，荊、襄蝗，米斗錢三千，人相食；

translations.literal: In the second year, locusts in Jing and Xiang; a dou of grain cost three thousand cash; men ate one another;
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 2 (888), Jing and Xiang suffered locusts; grain sold at three thousand cash per dou, and people fed on one another;

sentences.zh: 淮南蝗，自西來，行而不飛，浮水緣城入揚州府署，竹樹幢節，一夕如剪，幡幟畫像，皆齧去其首，撲不能止。

translations.literal: locusts in Huainan came from the west, going without flying, floating on water along the wall into the Yangzhou prefectural seat; bamboo, trees, banners, and ceremonial staffs—overnight as if clipped; flags and portraits—all gnawed away at the head; beating could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: in Huainan locusts came from the west, advancing without flying, floating on the water along the city wall into the Yangzhou prefectural offices; bamboo groves, trees, banners, and ceremonial insignia were shorn overnight as if clipped; painted banners and icons had their heads gnawed off, and beating could not drive them away.

sentences.zh: 旬日，自相食盡。

translations.literal: In ten days they had eaten one another to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days they had devoured one another to the last.

sentences.zh: 豕禍貞觀十七年六月，司農寺豕生子，一首八足，自頸分為二。

translations.literal: Swine calamity: In the sixth month of the seventeenth year of Zhenguan, a sow at the Directorate of Agriculture farrowed piglets with one head and eight legs, from the neck dividing into two.
translations.idiomatic: Swine calamities. In the sixth month of Zhenguan 17 (643), a sow at the Directorate of Agriculture farrowed piglets with one head and eight legs, split from the neck into two bodies.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年二月，京師民家有豕生子，兩首四足。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, at a commoner's house in the capital a sow farrowed piglets with two heads and four legs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhenyuan 4 (788), at a commoner's house in the capital a sow farrowed piglets with two heads and four legs.

sentences.zh: 首多者，上不一也。

translations.literal: Many heads signify disharmony above.
translations.idiomatic: Many heads betoken lack of unity at the top.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宣州大雨震電，有物墮地如猪，手足各兩指，執赤班蛇食之。

translations.literal: That year, in Xu Prefecture great rain, thunder, and lightning; a thing fell to earth like a pig, hands and feet each with two fingers, grasping a red-banded serpent and eating it.
translations.idiomatic: That year at Xu Prefecture came torrential rain with thunder and lightning; something fell to earth like a pig, with two fingers on each hand and foot, clutching a red-banded serpent and devouring it.

sentences.zh: 頃之，雲合不復見。

translations.literal: Shortly clouds joined and it was seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later clouds closed in and it was seen no more.

sentences.zh: 近豕禍也。

translations.literal: Close to a swine calamity.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a swine calamity.

sentences.zh: 元和八年四月，長安西市有豕生子，三耳八足，自尾分為二。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Yuanhe, at Chang'an's West Market a sow farrowed piglets with three ears and eight legs, from the tail dividing into two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanhe 8 (813), at Chang'an's West Market a sow farrowed piglets with three ears and eight legs, split from the tail into two.

sentences.zh: 足多者，下不一也。

translations.literal: Many legs signify disharmony below.
translations.idiomatic: Many legs betoken lack of unity below.

sentences.zh: 咸通七年，徐州蕭縣民家豕出圂舞，又牡豕多將隣里羣豕而行，復自相噬齧。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiantong, at a commoner's house in Xiao County of Xu Prefecture pigs came out of the sty and danced; also boars often led the neighborhood herd of pigs about, then again bit and devoured one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 7 (866), at a commoner's house in Xiaoxian, Xuzhou, pigs burst from the pen and danced; boars repeatedly led the neighborhood herds about, then turned and tore one another apart.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年，越州山陰民家有豕入室內，壞器用，銜桉缶置於水次。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianfu, at a commoner's house in Shanyin, Yue Prefecture, a pig entered the dwelling, broke utensils, and gripping a case and jar set them by the water's edge.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 6 (879), at a commoner's house in Shanyin, Yuezhou, a pig entered the rooms, smashed household goods, then seized a desk and jar and set them at the water's edge.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年，絳州稷山縣民家豕生如人狀，無眉目耳髮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangming, at a commoner's house in Jishan County, Jiang Prefecture, a sow bore young in human form, without eyebrows, eyes, ears, or hair.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangming 1 (880), at a commoner's house in Jishan, Jiangzhou, a sow bore young shaped like humans, lacking eyebrows, eyes, ears, or hair.

sentences.zh: 占為邑有亂。

translations.literal: The omen read: turmoil in the district.
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read as unrest in the district.

sentences.zh: 雷電貞觀十一年四月甲子，震乾元殿前槐樹。

translations.literal: Thunder and lightning: On the first jiazi of the fourth month of the eleventh year of Zhenguan, thunder struck the pagoda tree before Qianyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder and lightning. On the first jiazi of the fourth month of Zhenguan 11 (637), thunder struck the pagoda tree before Qianyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 震耀，天之威怒，以象殺戮；

translations.literal: Thunder's flare is Heaven's wrathful anger, emblematizing slaughter;
translations.idiomatic: The flare of thunder is Heaven's wrath, an image of slaughter;

sentences.zh: 槐，古者三公所樹也。

translations.literal: the pagoda tree—in antiquity it was what the Three Ducal Ministers planted.
translations.idiomatic: the pagoda tree was what the Three Ducal Ministers of antiquity planted.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年正月丁酉，雷。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth dingyou of the first month of the first year of Zhensheng, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth dingyou of the first month of Zhensheng 1 (695), thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 雷者陽聲，出非其時，臣竊君柄之象。

translations.literal: Thunder is yang's sound; when it issues out of season, it is the image of ministers usurping the ruler's handle.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder is the voice of yang; when it rolls forth out of season, it images ministers seizing the sovereign's grip.

sentences.zh: 長安四年五月丁亥，震雷，大風拔木，人有震死者。

translations.literal: On the seventh dinghai of the fifth month of the fourth year of Chang'an, thunder and great wind uprooted trees; some were struck dead by thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh dinghai of the fifth month of Chang'an 4 (704), thunder pealed and great winds uprooted trees; some people were struck dead by thunder.

sentences.zh: 延和元年六月，河南偃師縣李材村有震電入民家，地震裂，闊丈餘，長十五里，深不可測，所裂處井廁相通，或衝冢墓，柩出平地無損。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yanhe, at Licun, Yanshi County, Henan, thunder and lightning entered a commoner's house; the earth quaked and split, more than a zhang wide, fifteen li long, depth immeasurable; where it split, wells and privies interconnected, or smashed tombs—the coffins came out onto level ground unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yanhe 1 (712), at Licun in Yanshi, Henan, thunder and lightning entered a commoner's house; the earth quaked and split more than a zhang wide and fifteen li long to immeasurable depth; where it rent, wells and privies opened into one another, or tombs were breached—yet coffins emerged onto level ground unharmed.

sentences.zh: 李，國姓也；

translations.literal: Li—the surname of the state;
translations.idiomatic: Li—the royal surname;

sentences.zh: 震電，威刑之象；

translations.literal: thunder and lightning, the image of stern punishment;
translations.idiomatic: thunder and lightning image stern punishment;

sentences.zh: 地，陰類也。

translations.literal: earth belongs to the yin category.
translations.idiomatic: earth belongs to the category of yin.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年二月甲子夜，震霆。

translations.literal: On the first jiazi night of the second month of the first year of Yongtai, thunder and peals.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi night of the second month of Yongtai 1 (765), thunder pealed.

sentences.zh: 自是無雷，至六月甲申乃雷。

translations.literal: From then there was no thunder until the jiazi of the sixth month, then thunder.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the jiazi of the sixth month of Yongtai 1 there was no thunder, and only then did it thunder again.

sentences.zh: 大曆十年四月甲申，雷電，暴風拔木飄瓦，人有震死者，京畿害稼者七縣。

translations.literal: On the jiazi of the fourth month of the tenth year of Dali, thunder and lightning, violent wind uprooting trees and blowing off tiles; some struck dead by thunder; in seven counties of the capital region the harvest was harmed.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi of the fourth month of Dali 10 (775), thunder and lightning brought violent winds that uprooted trees and blew off tiles; some were struck dead by thunder; in seven counties of the capital region the harvest was harmed.

sentences.zh: 建中元年九月己卯，雷。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh jimao of the ninth month of the first year of Jianzhong, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh jimao of the ninth month of Jianzhong 1 (780), thunder sounded.

sentences.zh: 四年四月丙子，東都畿汝節度使哥舒曜攻李希烈，進軍至潁橋，大雨震電，人不能言者十三四，馬驢多死。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth bingzi of the fourth month of the fourth year, Geshu Yao of the Dongdu Jizhou Runan Circuit attacked Li Xilie, advancing the army to Yingqiao; great rain, thunder, and lightning—of the men, three or four tenths could not speak; many horses and donkeys died.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth bingzi of the fourth month of Jianzhong 4 (783), Geshu Yao of the Dongdu Jizhou Runan Circuit attacked Li Xilie and marched to Yingqiao; under great rain with thunder and lightning, three or four tenths of the men could not speak, and horses and donkeys died in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年五月己酉夏至，始雷。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice on the ninth jiyou of the fifth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, thunder first sounded.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice on the ninth jiyou of the fifth month of Zhenyuan 14 (798), thunder sounded for the first time.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年冬，雷。

translations.literal: In winter of the eleventh year of Yuanhe, thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yuanhe 11 (816), thunder rolled.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年六月乙丑，大風震電，落太廟鴟尾，破御史臺樹。

translations.literal: On the second yichou of the sixth month of the second year of Changqing, great wind, thunder, and lightning; the tail of the imperial temple's ridge ornament fell; the Censorate's trees were broken.
translations.idiomatic: On the second yichou of the sixth month of Changqing 2 (822), great winds with thunder and lightning stripped the imperial temple's ridge ornament and broke the trees of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 大和八年七月辛酉，定陵臺大雨，震，廡下地裂二十有六步。

translations.literal: On the ninth xinyou of the seventh month of the eighth year of Dahe, great rain at Dingling Terrace, thunder; the gallery's ground split twenty-six paces.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth xinyou of the seventh month of Dahe 8 (834), heavy rain at Dingling Terrace brought thunder; the gallery's ground split twenty-six paces.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「士庶分離，大臣專恣，不救大敗。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The nobles and commoners separate; great ministers act willfully; none will rescue—the great defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "When nobles and commoners sunder, when great ministers act willfully, and none turn back the tide—the state suffers great defeat."

sentences.zh: 會昌三年五月甲午，始雷。

translations.literal: On the eleventh jiawu of the fifth month of the third year of Huichang, thunder first.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh jiawu of the fifth month of Huichang 3 (843), thunder sounded for the first time.

sentences.zh: 咸通四年十二月，震雷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year of Xiantong, thunder and lightning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Xiantong 4 (863), thunder and lightning.

sentences.zh: 乾符二年十二月，震雷，雨雹。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Qianfu, thunder and lightning, hail.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Qianfu 2 (875), thunder, lightning, and hail.

sentences.zh: 乾寧四年，李茂貞遣將符道昭攻成都，至廣漢，震雷，有石隕于帳前。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qianning, Li Maozhen sent the general Fu Daozhao to attack Chengdu; reaching Guanghan, thunder and lightning; a stone fell before the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianning 4 (897), Li Maozhen sent the general Fu Daozhao to attack Chengdu; at Guanghan, thunder and lightning struck, and a stone fell before the command tent.

sentences.zh: 霜貞觀元年秋，霜殺稼。

translations.literal: Frost: In autumn of the first year of Zhenguan, frost killed the grain.
translations.idiomatic: Frost. In the autumn of Zhenguan 1 (627), frost killed the harvest.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「人君刑罰妄行，則天應之以隕霜。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the ruler capriciously enforces punishments, Heaven responds with falling frost."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes states: "When the ruler capriciously enforces punishments, Heaven answers with falling frost."

sentences.zh: 三年，北邊霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the third year, frost on the northern borderlands killed the grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629), frost on the northern borderlands killed the harvest.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，綏、延等州霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui, in Sui, Yan, and other circuits frost killed the grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 (651), frost killed the harvest in Sui, Yan, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 調露元年八月，邠、涇、寧、慶、原五州霜。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tiaolu, frost in Bin, Jing, Ning, Qing, and Yuan—the five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tiaolu 1 (679), frost struck the five prefectures of Bin, Jing, Ning, Qing, and Yuan.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年|695年六月，睦州隕霜，殺草。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Zhensheng |695 year|, at Mu Prefecture falling frost killed grass.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhensheng 1 |695 CE|, frost fell at Muzhou and killed the grass.

sentences.zh: 吳、越地燠而盛夏隕霜，昔所未有。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue lands are hot, yet in midsummer falling frost—never before seen.
translations.idiomatic: The lands of Wu and Yue are sultry, yet in midsummer frost fell—something never before recorded.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，延州霜殺草。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Yan Prefecture frost killed grass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhensheng 4 (697), frost at Yanzhou killed the grass.

sentences.zh: 四月純陽用事，象人君當布惠于天下，而反隕霜，是無陽也。

translations.literal: The fourth month is when pure yang holds sway, imaging that the ruler should spread grace throughout the realm, yet instead falling frost—this is absence of yang.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth month is when pure yang holds sway, imaging that the ruler should spread grace throughout the realm; yet frost fell instead—an absence of yang.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年八月，潞、綏等州霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, frost killed crops in Lu, Sui, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kaiyuan 12 (724), frost killed crops in Lu, Sui, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十五年，天下州十七，霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, frost killed crops in seventeen prefectures throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 (727), frost killed crops in seventeen prefectures throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 元和二年七月，邠、寧等州霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanhe, frost killed crops in Bin, Ning, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yuanhe 2 (807), frost killed crops in Bin, Ning, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 九年三月丁卯，隕霜，殺桑。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao of the third month of the ninth year, falling frost killed mulberry trees.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day in the third month of Yuanhe 9 (814), falling frost killed mulberry trees.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，淄、青隕霜，殺惡草及荊棘，而不害嘉穀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourteenth year, in Zi and Qing falling frost killed evil grasses and brambles but did not harm fine grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanhe 14 (819), falling frost in Zi and Qing killed weeds and brambles but spared the good grain.

sentences.zh: 寶曆元年八月，邠州霜殺稼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Baoli, frost killed crops in Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Baoli 1 (825), frost killed crops in Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大和三年秋，京畿奉先等八縣早霜，殺稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Dahe, early frost in eight counties of the capital region including Fengxian killed crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Dahe 3 (829), early frost in eight capital counties including Fengxian killed crops.

sentences.zh: 大中三年春，隕霜，殺桑。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Dazhong, falling frost killed mulberry trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Dazhong 3 (849), falling frost killed mulberry trees.

sentences.zh: 中和元年春，霜。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Zhonghe, frost.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Zhonghe 1 (881), frost appeared.

sentences.zh: 秋，河東早霜，殺稼。

translations.literal: In autumn, early frost in Hedong killed crops.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, early frost in Hedong killed crops.

sentences.zh: 雹貞觀四年秋，丹、延、北永等州雹。

translations.literal: Hail. In the autumn of the fourth year of Zhenguan, hail in Dan, Yan, Beiyong, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hail. In the autumn of Zhenguan 4 (630), hail struck Dan, Yan, Beiyong, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年五月，滄州大雨雹，中人有死者。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Xianqing, a great hailstorm in Cang Prefecture; among the people some died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xianqing 2 (657), a great hailstorm struck Cang Prefecture, and some among the populace were killed.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年四月庚午，雍州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the fourth month of the first year of Xianheng, a great hailstorm in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the fourth month of Xianheng 1 (670), a great hailstorm struck Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年四月戊子，大雨雹，震電，大風折木，落則天門鴟尾三。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi of the fourth month of the second year, a great hailstorm, lightning, and a great wind that broke trees; three Zetian Gate ridge-tail ornaments fell.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day in the fourth month of Xianheng 2 (671), heavy hail, lightning, and a great wind broke trees and knocked three ridge-tail ornaments from Zetian Gate.

sentences.zh: 先儒以為「雹者，陰脅陽也」。

translations.literal: The ancient scholars held that "Hail is yin constraining yang."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars held that "Hail means yin constraining yang."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「人君惡聞其過，抑賢用邪，則雹與雨俱；

translations.literal: It also says: "When the ruler hates to hear his faults, suppresses the worthy and employs the wicked, then hail comes together with rain;
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "When a ruler hates to hear his faults, suppresses the worthy and employs the wicked, hail falls together with rain;

sentences.zh: 信讒殺無罪，則雹下毀瓦、破車、殺牛馬。」

translations.literal: if one trusts slander and kills the guiltless, then hail falls, destroying tiles, breaking carts, and killing oxen and horses."
translations.idiomatic: if he trusts slander and kills the guiltless, hail destroys tiles, breaks carts, and kills oxen and horses."

sentences.zh: 永淳元年五月壬寅，定州大雨雹，害麥禾及桑。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the fifth month of the first year of Yongchun, a great hailstorm in Ding Prefecture harmed wheat, grain, and mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the fifth month of Yongchun 1 (682), a great hailstorm in Ding Prefecture damaged wheat, grain, and mulberry.

sentences.zh: 天授二年六月庚戌，許州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu of the sixth month of the second year of Tianshou, a great hailstorm in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day in the sixth month of Tianshou 2 (691), a great hailstorm struck Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年二月癸卯，滑州大雨雹，殺燕雀。

translations.literal: On the day guimao of the second month of the first year of Zhensheng, a great hailstorm in Hua Prefecture killed swallows and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day in the second month of Zhensheng 1 (695), a great hailstorm in Hua Prefecture killed swallows and sparrows.

sentences.zh: 神功元年，媯、綏二州雹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shendong, hail in Gui and Sui, two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Shendong 1 (697), hail struck the two prefectures of Gui and Sui.

sentences.zh: 聖曆元年六月甲午，曹州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the sixth month of the first year of Shenglü, a great hailstorm in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the sixth month of Shenglü 1 (698), a great hailstorm struck Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久視元年六月丁亥，曹州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the sixth month of the first year of Jiushi, a great hailstorm in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the sixth month of Jiushi 1 (700), a great hailstorm struck Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長安三年八月，京師大雨雹，人畜有凍死者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Chang'an, a great hailstorm in the capital; among people and livestock some froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chang'an 3 (703), a great hailstorm in the capital left some people and livestock frozen dead.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年四月壬子，雍州同官縣大雨雹，殺鳥獸。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of the fourth month of the first year of Shenlong, a great hailstorm in Tongguan County, Yong Prefecture, killed birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day in the fourth month of Shenlong 1 (705), a great hailstorm in Tongguan County, Yong Prefecture, killed birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 景龍元年四月己巳，曹州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day jisi of the fourth month of the first year of Jinglong, a great hailstorm in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day in the fourth month of Jinglong 1 (707), a great hailstorm struck Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年正月己卯，滄州雨雹如雞卵。

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the first month of the second year, hail in Cang Prefecture like chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the first month of Jinglong 2 (708), hail in Cang Prefecture was the size of chicken eggs.

sentences.zh: 開元八年十二月丁未，滑州大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei of the twelfth month of the eighth year of Kaiyuan, a great hailstorm in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day in the twelfth month of Kaiyuan 8 (720), a great hailstorm struck Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十二年五月戊辰，京畿渭南等六縣大風雹，傷麥。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen of the fifth month of the twenty-second year, wind and hail in six counties of the capital region including Weinan harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day in the fifth month of Kaiyuan 22 (734), wind and hail in six capital counties including Weinan damaged wheat.

sentences.zh: 大曆七年五月乙酉，雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou of the fifth month of the seventh year of Dali, hail.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day in the fifth month of Dali 7 (772), hail fell.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年六月丙子，大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi of the sixth month of the second year of Zhenyuan, a great hailstorm.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the sixth month of Zhenyuan 2 (786), a great hailstorm fell.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月丁酉，雨雹；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the second month of the seventeenth year, hail;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day in the second month of Zhenyuan 17 (801), hail fell;

sentences.zh: 己亥，霜；

translations.literal: on the day jihai, frost;
translations.idiomatic: on jihai day, frost;

sentences.zh: 戊申，夜，震霆，雨雹；

translations.literal: on the day wushen, at night, thunder and hail;
translations.idiomatic: on wushen night, thunder and hail;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，大雨雪而雹。

translations.literal: on the day gengxu, a great rain of snow with hail.
translations.idiomatic: on gengxu day, driving snow fell together with hail.

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅，好畤縣風雹，害麥。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the fifth month, wind and hail in Haozhi County harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day in the fifth month of Zhenyuan 17 (801), wind and hail in Haozhi County damaged wheat.

sentences.zh: 十八年七月癸酉，大雨雹。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou of the seventh month of the eighteenth year, a great hailstorm.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day in the seventh month of Zhenyuan 18 (802), a great hailstorm fell.

sentences.zh: 元和元年，鄜、坊等州雹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanhe, hail in Fu, Fang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 1 (806), hail struck Fu, Fang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十年秋，鄜、坊等州風雹，害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the tenth year, wind and hail in Fu, Fang, and other prefectures harmed crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Yuanhe 10 (815), wind and hail in Fu, Fang, and other prefectures damaged crops.

sentences.zh: 十二年夏，河南雨雹，中人有死者。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twelfth year, hail in Henan; among the people some died.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yuanhe 12 (817), hail in Henan killed some among the populace.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，京畿興平、醴泉等縣雹，傷麥。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, hail in counties of the capital region including Xingping and Liquan harmed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yuanhe 15 (820), hail in capital counties including Xingping and Liquan damaged wheat.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年六月庚寅，京師雨雹如彈丸。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the sixth month of the fourth year of Changqing, hail in the capital like pellet balls.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day in the sixth month of Changqing 4 (824), hail in the capital was the size of pellet balls.

sentences.zh: 大和四年秋，鄜、坊等州雹。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year of Dahe, hail in Fu, Fang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Dahe 4 (830), hail struck Fu, Fang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，京畿奉先、渭南等縣雨雹。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year, hail in counties of the capital region including Fengxian and Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Dahe 5 (831), hail fell in capital counties including Fengxian and Weinan.

sentences.zh: 開成二年秋，河南雹，害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Kaicheng, hail in Henan harmed crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kaicheng 2 (837), hail in Henan damaged crops.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，鄭、滑等州風雹。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, wind and hail in Zheng, Hua, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaicheng 4 (839), wind and hail struck Zheng, Hua, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，濮州雨雹如拳，殺人三十六，牛馬甚眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, hail in Pu Prefecture like fists, killing thirty-six people and a great many oxen and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kaicheng 5 (840), fist-sized hail in Pu Prefecture killed thirty-six people and a great many oxen and horses.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年秋，登州雨雹，文登尤甚，破瓦害稼。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Huichang, hail in Deng Prefecture; Wendeng was worst hit, tiles were broken and crops harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Huichang 1 (841), hail in Deng Prefecture—Wendeng suffered worst—breaking tiles and damaging crops.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，雨雹如彈丸。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year, hail like pellet balls.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Huichang 4 (844), hail fell the size of pellet balls.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年五月丁酉，宣授宰臣豆盧瑑、崔沆制，殿庭氛霧四塞，及百官班賀于政事堂，雨雹如鳧卵，大風雷雨拔木。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the fifth month of the sixth year of Qianfu, when edicts were announced appointing chief ministers Dou Lumiao and Cui Hang, mist and vapor blocked the hall on four sides; when the hundred officials formed ranks to congratulate at the Hall for Affairs of State, hail like duck eggs fell, and great wind, thunder, and rain uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day in the fifth month of Qianfu 6 (879), as edicts went forth appointing chief ministers Dou Lumiao and Cui Hang, mist closed in on all sides of the palace hall; when the hundred officials lined up to offer congratulations at the Hall for Affairs of State, hail fell the size of duck eggs, and fierce wind, thunder, and rain uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年四月甲申朔，汝州大雨風，拔街衢樹十二三；

translations.literal: On the first day jiashen of the fourth month of the first year of Guangming, great rain and wind in Ruzhou uprooted a dozen or so trees along the streets;
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the month, jiashen, in the fourth month of Guangming 1 (880), heavy rain and wind in Ruzhou uprooted twelve or thirteen trees along the avenues;

sentences.zh: 東都有雲起西北，大風隨之，長夏門內表道古槐樹自拔者十五六，宮殿鴟尾皆落，雨雹大如杯，鳥獸殪於川澤。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital clouds arose in the northwest, and great wind followed; within Changxia Gate along the ceremonial avenue fifteen or sixteen ancient locust trees uprooted themselves, the palace hall finial ornaments all fell, hail large as cups, birds and beasts perished in streams and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Capital clouds billowed from the northwest, followed by a great gale; inside Changxia Gate along the ceremonial avenue fifteen or sixteen ancient locust trees tore themselves from the earth, every finial on the palace halls crashed down, hail fell as large as cups, and birds and beasts perished in rivers and marshes.

sentences.zh: 黑眚黑祥大曆二年十二月戊戌，黑氣如塵，彌漫于北方。

translations.literal: Black omens and black auspices—on the day wuxu of the twelfth month of the second year of Dali, black vapor like dust spread throughout the north.
translations.idiomatic: Black omens and black auspices—On wuxu day in the twelfth month of Dali 2 (767), black vapor like dust spread across the northern sky.

sentences.zh: 黑氣，陰沴也。

translations.literal: Black vapor is yin injuring.
translations.idiomatic: Black vapor is the mark of yin forces violating their proper balance.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年七月，自陝至河陰，河水黑，流入汴，至汴州城下，一宿而復。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Zhenyuan, from Shan to Heyin the river water was black, flowed into the Bian, reached below Bianzhou city, and after one night returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhenyuan 4 (788), from Shan to Heyin the river water turned black, flowed into the Bian Canal, reached the walls of Bianzhou, and after one night reverted.

sentences.zh: 近黑祥也。

translations.literal: Near to black auspices.
translations.idiomatic: This approached a black auspice.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「法嚴刑酷，傷水性也。

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "When the law is severe and punishments cruel, it injures the nature of water.
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "Harsh laws and cruel punishments wound the element of water.

sentences.zh: 五行變節，陰陽相干，氣色繆亂，皆敗亂之象。」

translations.literal: The Five Phases change their seasons, yin and yang interact in conflict, vapors and colors are disordered and confused—all are images of defeat and disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Phases lose their proper seasons, yin and yang clash, qi and color fall into chaos—these are all signs of ruin and rebellion."

sentences.zh: 十四年，潤州有黑氣如隄，自海門山橫亙江中，與北固山相峙，又有白氣如虹自金山出，與黑氣交，將旦而沒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Runzhou had black vapor like a dike, from Haimen Mountain stretching across the river, facing Beigu Mountain across, and also white vapor like a rainbow emerging from Jinshan, intersecting with the black vapor, disappearing as dawn approached.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (798), Runzhou saw black vapor like an earthen dike stretch from Haimen Mountain across the river to stand opposite Beigu Mountain; white vapor like a rainbow rose from Jinshan and crossed the black vapor, then faded at dawn.

sentences.zh: 大和四年正月壬寅，黑氣如帶，東西際天。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the first month of the fourth year of Dahe, black vapor like a belt reached from east to west to the horizon.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day in the first month of Dahe 4 (830), a belt of black vapor stretched from horizon to horizon, east to west.

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年七月，僖宗即位，是日，黑氣如盤，自天屬含元殿庭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong, Emperor Xizong took the throne; that day, black vapor like a platter descended from heaven to touch the courtyard of Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xiantong 14 (873), as Emperor Xizong took the throne, black vapor like a platter descended from the sky onto the courtyard of Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 火沴水武德九年二月，蒲州河清。

translations.literal: Fire injuring water—in the second month of the ninth year of Wude, the river at Puzhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: Fire injuring water—In the second month of Wude 9 (626), the river at Puzhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 襄楷以為：「河，諸侯象；

translations.literal: Xiang Kai held: "The river is the image of feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Kai held that "the river symbolizes the feudal lords;

sentences.zh: 清，陽明之效也。」

translations.literal: clarity is the effect of yang brightness."
translations.idiomatic: and clarity is the manifestation of yang's radiant virtue."

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年二月，陝州、泰州河清。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, the rivers at Shanzhou and Taizhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhenguan 14 (640), the rivers at Shanzhou and Taizhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，懷州河清。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year, the river at Huaizhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenguan 16 (642), the river at Huaizhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 十七年十二月，鄭州、滑州河清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventeenth year, the rivers at Zhengzhou and Huazhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhenguan 17 (643), the rivers at Zhengzhou and Huazhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 二十三年四月，靈州河清。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year, the river at Lingzhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenguan 23 (649), the river at Lingzhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年正月，濟州河清。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yonghui, the river at Jizhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yonghui 1 (650), the river at Jizhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 二年十二月，衞州河清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year, the river at Weizhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Yonghui 2 (651), the river at Weizhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，濟州河清十六里。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, the river at Jizhou ran clear for sixteen li.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yonghui 5 (654), the river at Jizhou ran clear for sixteen li.

sentences.zh: 調露二年夏，豐州河清。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Tiaolu, the river at Fengzhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tiaolu 2 (679), the river at Fengzhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 長安初，醴泉坊太平公主第井水溢流。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chang'an, the well water at Princess Taiping's residence in Liquan Ward overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Chang'an era (701), the well at Princess Taiping's mansion in Liquan Ward overflowed.

sentences.zh: 又幷州文水縣猷水竭，武氏井溢。

translations.literal: Also in Bingzhou, the You River in Wenshui County dried up, and the Wu clan well overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In Bingzhou the You River in Wenshui County ran dry while a well belonging to the Wu clan brimmed over.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年三月壬子，洛陽城東七里，地色如水，樹木車馬，歷歷見影，漸移至都，月餘乃滅。

translations.literal: On the day renzi of the third month of the second year of Shenlong, seven li east of Luoyang city, the ground's color was like water—trees, carriages, and horses, their shadows all clearly visible, gradually shifting toward the capital; after more than a month it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day in the third month of Shenlong 2 (706), seven li east of Luoyang the ground shone like water, with trees, carriages, and horses casting shadows as clear as reflections; the phenomenon crept toward the capital and did not fade for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 長安街中，往往見水影。

translations.literal: In the streets of Chang'an, water-shadows were often seen.
translations.idiomatic: In the streets of Chang'an, phantom water reflections appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 昔苻堅之將死也，長安嘗有是。

translations.literal: Formerly when Fu Jian was about to die, Chang'an once had this.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Fu Jian was nearing his death, the same sign had appeared in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 景龍四年三月庚申，京師井水溢。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen of the third month of the fourth year of Jinglong, wells in the capital overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the third month of Jinglong 4 (710), wells throughout the capital brimmed over.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「君凶。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The ruler is in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "The ruler faces disaster."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「兵將起。」

translations.literal: It further states: "Armies are about to rise."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "Armies are about to rise."

sentences.zh: 開元二十二年八月，清夷軍黃帝祠古井湧浪。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-second year of Kaiyuan, the ancient well at the Yellow Emperor shrine in Qingyi Army garrison surged with waves.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kaiyuan 22 (734), the ancient well at the Yellow Emperor shrine in Qingyi Army district heaved with surging waves.

sentences.zh: 二十五年五月，淄州、棣州河清。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twenty-fifth year, the rivers at Zizhou and Dizhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 25 (737), the rivers at Zizhou and Dizhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，亳州老子祠九井涸復湧。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, at Bozhou Lao Zi's shrine, nine wells dried up then surged again.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 (741), nine wells at the shrine of Laozi in Bozhou ran dry and then welled up again.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年七月，嵐州合河關河三十里清如井水，四日而變。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Qianyuan, at Lanzhou's Hehe Pass the river for thirty li was clear as well water, changing after four days.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Qianyuan 2 (759), the river at Hehe Pass in Lanzhou ran as clear as well water for thirty li, then within four days reverted.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年九月甲午，太州至陝州二百餘里河清，澄澈見底。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu of the ninth month of the first year of Baoying, from Taizhou to Shanzhou for more than two hundred li the river ran clear, limpid enough to see the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day in the ninth month of Baoying 1 (762), the river from Taizhou to Shanzhou ran clear for more than two hundred li, so limpid one could see the bottom.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，深州束鹿縣中有水影長七八尺，遙望見人馬往來，如在水中，及至前，則不見水。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, in Shulu County of Shenzhou there were water-shadows seven or eight chi long; gazing from afar one saw people and horses coming and going as if in water, but approaching close, no water was to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Dali reign (779–780), Shulu County in Shenzhou produced phantom water reflections seven or eight feet long; from a distance people and horses seemed to move through water, yet up close there was no water at all.

sentences.zh: 建中四年五月乙巳，滑州、濮州河清。

translations.literal: On the day yisi of the fifth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, the rivers at Huazhou and Puzhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the fifth month of Jianzhong 4 (783), the rivers at Huazhou and Puzhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年閏五月乙丑，滑州河清。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the intercalary fifth month of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan, the river at Huazhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day in the intercalary fifth month of Zhenyuan 14 (798), the river at Huazhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 二十一年夏，越州鏡湖竭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-first year, Mirror Lake in Yuezhou dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenyuan 21 (805), Mirror Lake in Yuezhou dried up.

sentences.zh: 是歲，朗州熊、武五溪水鬬。

translations.literal: That year, in Langzhou the waters of the Xiong and Wu rivulets of Wuxi fought.
translations.idiomatic: That same year in Langzhou the Xiong and Wu branches of the Wuxi River clashed—their currents colliding as if at war.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「山崩川竭，國必亡。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "When mountains collapse and rivers dry up, the state will surely perish."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "When mountains collapse and rivers run dry, the state is doomed."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「方伯力政，厥異水鬬。」

translations.literal: It further states: "When regional lords enforce government by force, the anomaly is waters fighting."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "When regional lords impose their will by force, the portent is rivers at war with one another."

sentences.zh: 開成二年夏，旱，揚州運河竭。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Kaicheng, drought—the Grand Canal at Yangzhou dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaicheng 2 (837), during a drought the Grand Canal at Yangzhou ran dry.

sentences.zh: 大中八年正月，陝州河清。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Dazhong, the river at Shanzhou ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dazhong 8 (854), the river at Shanzhou ran clear.

sentences.zh: 咸通八年七月，泗州下邳雨湯，殺鳥雀。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xiantong, at Xiapi in Sizhou hot rain fell, killing birds and sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xiantong 8 (867), scorching rain fell at Xiapi in Sizhou and killed birds and sparrows.

sentences.zh: 水沸于火，則可以傷物，近火沴水也。

translations.literal: Water boiling from fire can then injure things—near to fire injuring water.
translations.idiomatic: When water boils at fire's touch it can harm living things—this approximates fire injuring water.

sentences.zh: 雨者，自上而降；

translations.literal: Rain — it descends from above;
translations.idiomatic: Rain falls from above;

sentences.zh: 鳥雀，民象。

translations.literal: birds and sparrows are the people's emblem.
translations.idiomatic: birds and sparrows symbolize the common people.

sentences.zh: 中和三年秋，汴水入于淮水鬬，壞船數艘。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year of Zhonghe, the Bian River entered the Huai and they contended; several vessels were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the third year of Zhonghe (883), the Bian and Huai clashed and destroyed several boats.

sentences.zh: 廣明元年夏，汝州峴陽峯龍池涸。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Guangming, the Dragon Pool on Xianyang Peak in Ru Prefecture dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the first year of Guangming (880), the Dragon Pool on Xianyang Peak in Ru Prefecture ran dry.

sentences.zh: 近川竭也。

translations.literal: A nearby river had run dry.
translations.idiomatic: This was a nearby river running dry.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「皇之不極，是謂不建。

translations.literal: The Wuxing Zhuan says: "When the sovereign fails to reach the extreme, it is called failure to establish.
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition of the Five Elements says: "When the sovereign fails to reach the ultimate mean, this is called failure to establish.

sentences.zh: 厥咎眊，厥罰常陰，厥極弱。

translations.literal: Its fault is dim-sightedness; its punishment is constant yin; its extreme is weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is dim-sightedness; the penalty is persistent gloom; the ultimate consequence is weakness.

sentences.zh: 時則有射妖，時則有龍蛇之孽，時則有馬禍，時則有下人伐上之痾，時則有日月亂行，星辰逆行。」

translations.literal: At such times there are shooting demons; at such times there are dragon-and-snake calamities; at such times there are horse portents; at such times there is the affliction of inferiors attacking superiors; at such times the sun and moon run in disorder and the stars move retrograde."
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons shooting demons appear, dragon-and-snake calamities arise, horse omens manifest, inferiors strike at superiors, the sun and moon lose their courses, and the stars move backward."

sentences.zh: 謂木金火水土沴天也。

translations.literal: This means the catastrophes of wood, metal, fire, water, and earth afflicting Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: That is, the calamities in which wood, metal, fire, water, and earth violate Heaven.

sentences.zh: 常陰長安四年，自九月霖雨陰晦，至于神龍元年正月。

translations.literal: Constant yin: In the fourth year of Chang'an, from the ninth month unceasing rain and gloom lasted until the first month of the first year of Shenlong.
translations.idiomatic: Persistent gloom: From the ninth month of the fourth year of Chang'an (704) until the first month of Shenlong 1 (705), rain and overcast skies persisted without break.

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年秋，連月陰霪。

translations.literal: In autumn of the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan, months on end of yin downpour.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan (805), unbroken rains darkened the months.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年正月庚辰至于丙申，晝常陰晦，微雨雪，夜則晴霽。

translations.literal: From gengchen through bingshen in the first month of the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, by day constant yin and gloom with light rain and snow; by night it cleared.
translations.idiomatic: From gengchen through bingshen in the first month of Yuanhe 15 (820), days stayed under persistent gloom with slight rain and snow while nights cleared.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「晝霧夜晴，臣志得申。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "Daytime mist/fog, nighttime clear — the minister's intent is fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "Mist by day and clear skies by night mean the minister's design will prevail."

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年七月，靈州陰晦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong, Ling Prefecture was overcast and gloomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Xiantong (873), Lingzhou lay under gloom.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年秋，多雲霧晦冥，自旦及禺中乃解。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year of Qianfu, clouds and mist made it dim from dawn until the second watch (9–11 a.m.), when it lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the sixth year of Qianfu (879), cloud and mist veiled the sky from dawn until mid-morning, then dispersed.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年秋，河東大雲霧。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Guangqi, great cloud-mist in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the first year of Guangqi (885), heavy mist shrouded Hedong.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，晝陰積六十日。

translations.literal: The next summer, daytime yin accumulated for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, dim days piled up for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 二年十一月，淮南陰晦雨雪，至明年二月不解。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, Huainan was gloomy with rain and snow until the second month of the next year without clearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Guangqi 2 (887), Huainan turned gloomy with rain and snow and did not lift until the second month of the next year.

sentences.zh: 景福二年夏，連陰四十餘日。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Jingfu, continuous yin for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the second year of Jingfu (893), unbroken overcast lasted more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 霧長壽元年九月戊戌，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: Mist/Fog: On the wuxu day of the ninth month of the first year of Changshou, yellow mist walled in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Mist: On wuxu in the ninth month of the first year of Changshou (694), yellow mist closed in on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 霧者，百邪之氣，為陰冒陽，本于地而應于天；

translations.literal: Mist is the qi of a hundred evils; yin overtops yang, rooted in earth and responding in heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Mist is the breath of a hundred malign forces: yin overspreads yang, springing from earth and answering in heaven;

sentences.zh: 黃為土，土為中宮。

translations.literal: Yellow is earth; earth is the Central Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow belongs to earth, and earth is the Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年三月乙巳，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: On the yisi day of the third month of the second year of Shenlong, yellow mist walled in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the third month of Shenlong 2 (706), yellow mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年八月甲戌，黃霧昏濁不雨。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day of the eighth month of the second year of Jinglong, yellow mist was murky and dim without rain.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu in the eighth month of Jinglong 2 (708), yellow mist hung murky and dim, yet no rain fell.

sentences.zh: 二年正月丁卯，黃霧四塞。

translations.literal: On the dingmao day of the first month of the second year, yellow mist walled in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao in the first month of Jinglong 2, yellow mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲寅，日入後，昏霧四塞，經二日乃止。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day of the eleventh month, after the sun had set, dusk mist walled in on every side; after two days it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin in the eleventh month, after sunset dusk mist sealed the four quarters and lasted two days before lifting.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「霧連日不解，其國昏亂。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "When mist persists for successive days without lifting, that state falls into confusion."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "When mist hangs day after day without dispersing, the realm sinks into disorder."

sentences.zh: 開元五年正月戊辰，昏霧四塞。

translations.literal: On the wuchen day of the first month of the fifth year of Kaiyuan, dusk mist walled in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the first month of Kaiyuan 5 (717), dusk mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載冬三月，常霧起昏暗，十步外不見人，是謂晝昏。

translations.literal: In winter of the third month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, mist continually rose, darkness and gloom; ten paces away one could not see a person — this is called daytime gloom.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third month of Tianbao 14 (755), mist kept rising until noon stayed dark: at ten paces one could not see another person. This is called daytime gloom.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「有破國。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "There will be a broken state."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "A realm will be broken."

sentences.zh: 至德二載四月，賊將武令珣圍南陽，白霧四塞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Zhide, the rebel general Wu Lingxun besieged Nanyang; white mist walled in on every side.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhide 2 (757), the rebel general Wu Lingxun besieged Nanyang, and white mist closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 上元元年閏四月，大霧。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fourth month of the first year of Shangyuan, great mist.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fourth month of Shangyuan 1 (760), a heavy mist fell.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兵起。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "Armies arise."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "War will arise."

sentences.zh: 貞元十年三月乙亥，黃霧四塞，日無光。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the third month of the tenth year of Zhenyuan, yellow mist walled in on every side, and the sun had no light.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai in the third month of Zhenyuan 10 (794), yellow mist sealed the four quarters and the sun lost its light.

sentences.zh: 咸通九年十一月，龐勛圍徐州，甲辰，大霧昏塞，至于丙午。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year of Xiantong, Pang Xun besieged Xuzhou; on jiachen a great mist darkened and walled in the land until bingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xiantong 9 (868), Pang Xun besieged Xuzhou; on jiachen a dense mist darkened the land until bingwu.

sentences.zh: 光化四年冬，昭宗在東內，武德門內煙霧四塞，門外日色皎然。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year of Guanghua, Emperor Zhaozong was in the Eastern Inner Palace; within the Wude Gate smoke and mist walled in on every side, while outside the gate the sunlight was bright.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of Guanghua 4 (901), with Emperor Zhaozong in the Eastern Inner Palace, smoke and mist sealed the four sides within the Wude Gate, yet outside the gate the sunlight shone clear.

sentences.zh: 虹蜺武德初，隋將堯君素守蒲州，有白虹下城中。

translations.literal: Rainbow: Early in Wude, the Sui general Yao Junsu held Pu Prefecture; a white rainbow descended into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Rainbow: Early in Wude (618), while the Sui general Yao Junsu held Pu Prefecture, a white rainbow descended into the city.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年六月戊子，虹蜺亙天。

translations.literal: On the wuzi day of the sixth month of the first year of Tanglong, a rainbow spanned heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi in the sixth month of Tanglong 1 (710), a rainbow stretched across the sky.

sentences.zh: 蜺者，斗之精。

translations.literal: The secondary bow (ni) is the essence of the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: The secondary arc is the essence of the Dipper constellation.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「后妃陰脅王者。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The queen and consorts will threaten the king by yin force."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "Queens and consorts will press upon the king through feminine power."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「五色迭至，照于宮殿，有兵。」

translations.literal: It also states: "When the five colors come in succession and shine upon the palace halls, there will be armies."
translations.idiomatic: It also states: "When the five colors appear in turn and light the palace halls, armies will rise."

sentences.zh: 延和元年六月，幽州都督孫佺帥兵襲奚，將入賊境，有白虹垂頭于軍門。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Yanhe, Youzhou Military Commissioner Sun Zhen led troops in a surprise strike against the Xi; as they were about to enter the enemy territory, a white rainbow hung its head at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yanhe 1 (712), Youzhou commissioner Sun Zhen led troops to raid the Xi; just as they were entering hostile ground, a white rainbow hung its head down at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「其下流血。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "Below it blood will flow."
translations.idiomatic: Prognostication states: "Blood will flow beneath it."

sentences.zh: 至德二載正月丙子，南陽夜有白虹四，上亙百餘丈。

translations.literal: On the bingzi day of the first month of the second year of Zhide, at night in Nanyang four white rainbows stood, each spanning more than a hundred zhang above.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the first month of Zhide 2 (757), four white rainbows at night in Nanyang stretched upward more than a hundred zhang.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年十二月丙辰，有白虹闊五尺，東西亙天。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day of the twelfth month of the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, a white rainbow five chi wide stretched east and west across heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the twelfth month of Yuanhe 13 (818), a white rainbow five chi wide arched from horizon to horizon.

sentences.zh: 會昌四年正月己酉，西方有白虹。

translations.literal: On the jiyou day of the first month of the fourth year of Huichang, in the west there was a white rainbow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the first month of Huichang 4 (844), a white rainbow appeared in the west.

sentences.zh: 咸通元年七月己酉朔，白虹橫亙西方。

translations.literal: On the first day jiyou of the seventh month of the first year of Xiantong, a white rainbow lay horizontally across the west.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day, jiyou, of the seventh month of Xiantong 1 (860), a white rainbow stretched across the western sky.

sentences.zh: 九年七月戊戌，白虹橫亙西方。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, on the wuxu day, a white rainbow lay horizontally across the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xiantong 9 (868), on wuxu day, a white rainbow again spanned the west.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年九月，白虹見西方。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Guangqi, a white rainbow appeared in the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guangqi 2 (886), a white rainbow was seen in the west.

sentences.zh: 十月壬辰夜，又如之。

translations.literal: On the night of renchen in the tenth month, it was again so.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renchen in the tenth month, the same omen appeared again.

sentences.zh: 天復三年三月庚申，有曲虹在日東北。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day of the third month of the third year of Tianfu, a curved rainbow was northeast of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the third month of Tianfu 3 (903), a curved rainbow stood northeast of the sun.

sentences.zh: 龍蛇孽貞觀八年七月，隴右大蛇屢見。

translations.literal: Dragon and snake calamities: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Zhenguan, in Longyou great snakes were repeatedly seen.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon and snake calamities: In the seventh month of Zhenguan 8 (634), great snakes were repeatedly sighted in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 蛇，女子之祥；

translations.literal: The snake is an auspice of woman;
translations.idiomatic: The snake is a woman's omen;

sentences.zh: 大者，有所象也。

translations.literal: when large, it has something it images.
translations.idiomatic: when it is large, it images some greater thing.

sentences.zh: 又汾州青龍見，吐物在空中，光明如火，墮地地陷，掘之得玄金，廣尺，長七寸。

translations.literal: Again at Fen Prefecture a blue dragon appeared, spewed something in midair bright as fire; it fell to earth and the ground sank; digging yielded dark metal a foot wide and seven inches long.
translations.idiomatic: At Fen Prefecture a blue dragon also appeared, vomiting something into the air that blazed like fire; when it struck the ground the earth collapsed, and excavation yielded a block of dark metal a foot wide and seven inches long.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年五月庚寅，有五龍見于岐州之皇后泉。

translations.literal: On the gengyin day of the fifth month of the second year of Xianqing, five dragons appeared at the Queen's Spring in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin in the fifth month of Xianqing 2 (657), five dragons were seen at the Queen's Spring in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先天二年六月，京師朝堂塼下有大蛇出，長丈餘，有大蝦蟆如盤，而目赤如火，相與鬬，俄而蛇入于大樹，蝦蟆入于草。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Xiantian, beneath the bricks of the capital audience hall a great snake emerged more than a zhang long; there was also a great toad like a tray, its eyes red as fire; they fought each other; presently the snake entered a great tree and the toad entered the grass.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Xiantian 2 (713), beneath the audience-hall paving stones in the capital a serpent more than a zhang long emerged, along with a tray-sized toad whose eyes burned red as coals; the two fought until the serpent slipped into a great tree and the toad into the grass.

sentences.zh: 蛇、蝦蟆，皆陰類；

translations.literal: Snake and toad are both yin kinds;
translations.idiomatic: Snake and toad alike belong to yin;

sentences.zh: 朝堂出，非其所也。

translations.literal: to emerge at the audience hall is not their place.
translations.idiomatic: yet to surface at the audience hall is to be far from their proper realm.

sentences.zh: 開元四年六月，郴州馬嶺山下有白蛇與黑蛇鬬，白蛇長六七尺，吞黑蛇，至腹，口眼血流，黑蛇長丈餘，頭穿白蛇腹出，俱死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Kaiyuan, below Mount Maling in Chen Prefecture a white snake and a black snake fought; the white snake was six or seven chi, swallowed the black snake to the belly, mouth and eyes streaming blood; the black snake was more than a zhang long, its head piercing out through the white snake's belly; both died.
