translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kaiyuan 4 (716), below Ma Ridge in Chenzhou, a white serpent six or seven chi long battled a black serpent. The white snake swallowed the black to its belly, blood streaming from mouth and eyes, until the black serpent—a full zhang and more—drove its head out through the white snake's belly; both died.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，洛陽有巨蛇，高丈餘，長百尺，出芒山下，胡僧無畏見之曰：「此欲決水瀦洛城。」

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, at Luoyang there was a huge snake more than a zhang high and a hundred chi long; it came out below Mang Mountain; the foreign monk Wuwei, seeing it, said: "This intends to breach the waters and flood Luoyang."
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign, a serpent rose below Mang Mountain at Luoyang, more than a zhang tall and a hundred chi long. The foreign monk Wuwei saw it and said, "It means to break the waters and drown Luoyang."

sentences.zh: 即以天竺法呪之，數日蛇死。

translations.literal: He thereupon used the Indian spell upon it; within days the snake died.
translations.idiomatic: He cast an Indian spell upon it, and within days the serpent was dead.

sentences.zh: 十四載七月，有二龍鬬于南陽城西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, two dragons fought west of Nanyang city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianbao 14 (755), two dragons fought west of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 易坤：「上六，龍戰于野。」

translations.literal: The Changes, Kun: "Top line: dragons battle in the wild."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes, Kun: "The top line: dragons battle in the wild."

sentences.zh: 文言曰：「陰疑于陽必戰。」

translations.literal: The Commentary on the Words states: "When yin grows doubtful of yang, battle is certain."
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Words says, "When yin grows doubtful of yang, battle is inevitable."

sentences.zh: 至德元載八月朔，成都丈人廟有肉角蛇見。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month of the first year of Zhide, at the Zhangren Shrine in Chengdu a fleshy-horned snake appeared.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month of Zhide 1 (756), a fleshy-horned serpent appeared at the Zhangren Shrine in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 二載三月，有蛇鬬于南陽門之外，一蛇死，一蛇上城。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, snakes fought outside the Nanyang Gate; one snake died and one climbed the wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhide 2 (757), serpents fought outside the Nanyang Gate; one died and one scaled the city wall.

sentences.zh: 建中二年夏，趙州寧晉縣沙河北，有棠樹甚茂，民祠之為神。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Jianzhong, north of the Sha River in Ningjin County, Zhao Prefecture, there was a crabapple tree very luxuriant; the people worshipped it as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jianzhong 2 (781), on the north bank of the Sha River at Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture, a crabapple tree grew extravagantly lush, and the people worshipped it as a god.

sentences.zh: 有蛇數百千自東西來，趨北岸者聚棠樹下，為二積，留南岸者為一積，俄有徑寸龜三，繞行，積蛇盡死，而後各登其積。

translations.literal: Several hundred or a thousand snakes came from east and west; those hurrying to the north bank gathered under the crabapple tree into two piles, while those remaining on the south bank made one pile; presently three tortoises of inch-girth circled about, the piled snakes all died, and afterward each climbed its pile.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds upon hundreds of serpents came from east and west. Those racing to the north bank heaped themselves in two mounds beneath the crabapple; those left on the south bank formed a third. Then three inch-wide tortoises circled the mounds until every serpent lay dead, after which each tortoise climbed its mound.

sentences.zh: 野人以告。

translations.literal: Rustics reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Country folk reported what they had seen.

sentences.zh: 蛇腹皆有瘡，若矢所中。

translations.literal: The snakes' bellies all had sores, as if struck by arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Every serpent's belly bore wounds as though pierced by arrows.

sentences.zh: 刺史康日知圖其事，奉三龜來獻。

translations.literal: Prefect Kang Rizhi diagrammed the affair and presented the three tortoises as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Kang Rizhi recorded the event and sent the three tortoises up as tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年九月戊寅，有龍見于汝州城壕。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day of the ninth month of the fourth year, a dragon appeared in the moat of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the ninth month of Jianzhong 4 (783), a dragon was seen in the moat of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 龍，大人象，其潛也淵，其飛也天；

translations.literal: The dragon is the image of the great man; in hiding it is the abyss, in flight it is heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The dragon images the great man: in hiding it belongs to the deep, in flight to heaven;

sentences.zh: 城壕，失其所也。

translations.literal: the city moat is losing its place.
translations.idiomatic: yet a city moat is nowhere for it to be.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，資州得龍丈餘，西川節度使韋臯匣而獻之，百姓縱觀，三日，為煙所薰而死。

translations.literal: Late in Zhenyuan, Zi Prefecture obtained a dragon more than a zhang long; the Xichuan military commissioner Wei Gao cased it and presented it; common people watched freely; in three days it died, suffocated by smoke.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Zhenyuan, Zizhou caught a dragon more than a zhang long. The Xichuan commissioner Wei Gao boxed it and sent it up; the people thronged to look for three days until smoke suffocated it to death.

sentences.zh: 大和二年六月丁丑，西北有龍鬬。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day of the sixth month of the second year of Dahe, in the northwest dragons fought.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the sixth month of Dahe 2 (828), dragons battled in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 三年，成都門外有龍與牛鬬。

translations.literal: In the third year, outside the Chengdu gate a dragon fought with an ox.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 3 (829), outside the Chengdu city gate a dragon fought an ox.

sentences.zh: 開成元年，宮中有眾蛇相與鬬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaicheng, within the palace many snakes fought one another.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 1 (836), a host of serpents battled one another inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 光化三年九月，杭州有龍鬬于浙江，水溢，壞民廬舍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Guanghua, at Hangzhou dragons fought on the Zhe River; the water overflowed and ruined the people's houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Guanghua 3 (900), at Hangzhou dragons fought on the Zhe River; the waters rose and wrecked the people's dwellings.

sentences.zh: 占同天寶十四載。

translations.literal: Prognostication matches the fourteenth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication matches Tianbao 14 (755).

sentences.zh: 光啟二年冬，鄜州洛交有蛇見于縣署，復見于州署。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Guangqi, at Luojiao in Fu Prefecture a snake appeared at the county office and again at the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Guangqi 2 (886), at Luojiao in Fuzhou a serpent appeared in the county yamen and again in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 蛇，冬則蟄，易曰：「龍蛇之蟄，以存身也。」

translations.literal: The snake in winter then hibernates; the Changes say: "The hibernation of dragon and snake is to preserve the body."
translations.idiomatic: Snakes hibernate in winter; the Changes say, "Dragon and snake hibernate to preserve the body."

sentences.zh: 馬禍義寧二年|618年五月戊申，有馬生角，長二寸，末有肉。

translations.literal: Horse calamity: On the wushen day of the fifth month of the second year of Yining |618 year|, a horse grew horns two inches long, with flesh at the tips.
translations.idiomatic: Horse calamities: On wushen in the fifth month of Yining 2 (618), a horse sprouted horns two inches long, fleshy at the tips.

sentences.zh: 角者，兵象。

translations.literal: Horns are the image of armies.
translations.idiomatic: Horns image armies.

sentences.zh: 武德三年十月，王世充偽左僕射韋霽馬生角，當項。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Wude, the false Left Vice Director Wei Ji of Wang Shichong's regime had a horse grow horns at the nape.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Wude 3 (620), Wei Ji, bogus Left Vice Director under Wang Shichong, had a horse grow horns at the nape.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，監牧馬大死，凡十八萬疋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, the imperial stud horses died in great numbers, altogether one hundred eighty thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong 2 (681), stud horses died in vast numbers—one hundred eighty thousand head in all.

sentences.zh: 馬者，國之武備，天去其備，國將危亡。

translations.literal: The horse is the state's martial readiness; when Heaven removes its readiness, the state will be imperiled and perish.
translations.idiomatic: Horses are the state's martial readiness; when Heaven strips that readiness away, the realm faces ruin.

sentences.zh: 文明初，新豐有馬生駒，二首同項，各有口鼻，生而死。

translations.literal: Early in Wenming, at Xinfeng a mare foaled, two heads on one neck, each with mouth and nostrils; it was born and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wenming (684), at Xinfeng a mare foaled twins with two heads on one neck, each bearing mouth and nostrils; the foal lived only to die.

sentences.zh: 又咸陽牝馬生石，大如升，上微有綠毛。

translations.literal: Again at Xianyang a mare produced stone the size of a sheng, with slight green hair on top.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianyang a mare also expelled a stone the size of a sheng, faintly tufted with green hair.

sentences.zh: 皆馬禍也。

translations.literal: All are horse calamities.
translations.idiomatic: All were horse calamities.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年五月，太原獻異馬駒，兩肋各十六，肉尾無毛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, Taiyuan presented a strange foal, sixteen ribs on each flank, a fleshy tail without hair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 12 (724), Taiyuan presented a strange foal with sixteen ribs on each flank and a fleshy, hairless tail.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，濮州有馬生駒，肉角。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, at Pu Prefecture a horse foaled, with fleshy horns.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 (737), at Puzhou a mare foaled a colt bearing fleshy horns.

sentences.zh: 二十九年三月，滑州刺史李邕獻馬，肉鬉鱗臆，嘶不類馬，日行三百里。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-ninth year, Li Yong, prefect of Huazhou, presented a horse with a fleshy mane and scaly chest; its neighing was unlike that of a horse, and it traveled three hundred li in a day.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 29, Li Yong, prefect of Huazhou, presented a horse with a fleshlike mane and scale-patterned breast; its cry was unlike any horse's, and it could travel three hundred li in a day.

sentences.zh: 建中四年五月，滑州馬生角。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Jianzhong, horses in Huazhou grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Jianzhong 4, horses in Huazhou grew horns.

sentences.zh: 大和九年八月，易定馬飲水，因吐珠一，以獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Dahe, horses in Yiding drank water and spat out a pearl, which was presented as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Dahe 9, horses in Yiding drank water and expelled a pearl, which was presented to the court.

sentences.zh: 開成元年六月，揚州民明齊家馬生角，長一寸三分。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Kaicheng, the horse of the commoner Ming Qi of Yangzhou grew a horn one cun and three fen long.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Kaicheng 1, a horse belonging to the Yangzhou commoner Ming Qi grew a horn one cun and three fen in length.

sentences.zh: 會昌元年四月，桂州有馬生駒，三足，能隨羣于牧。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Huichang, in Guizhou a mare foaled a colt with three legs that could follow the herd in pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Huichang 1, a Guizhou mare foaled a three-legged colt that could nonetheless follow the herd on the pasture.

sentences.zh: 咸通三年，郴州馬生角。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiantong, horses in Chenzhou grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 3, horses in Chenzhou grew horns.

sentences.zh: 十一年，沁州綿上及和川牡馬生子，皆死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, at Mianshang in Qinzhou and at Hechuan, stallions foaled, and all [the births] died.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 11, at Mianshang in Qinzhou and at Hechuan, stallions foaled, and all the births died.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「方伯分威，厥妖牡馬生子。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When regional lords divide authority, the omen is a stallion giving birth."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes states: "When regional lords divide power among themselves, the portent is a stallion that foals."

sentences.zh: 乾符二年，河北馬生人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfu, horses in Hebei gave birth to humans.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu 2, horses in Hebei gave birth to what appeared to be human infants.

sentences.zh: 中和元年九月，長安馬生人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Zhonghe, horses in Chang'an gave birth to humans.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhonghe 1, horses in Chang'an gave birth to human-shaped creatures.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「諸侯相伐，厥妖馬生人。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the feudal lords attack one another, the omen is a horse giving birth to a human."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes states: "When feudal lords make war upon one another, the portent is a horse that delivers a human."

sentences.zh: 一曰：「人流亡。」

translations.literal: One reading says: "The people flee and scatter."
translations.idiomatic: Another tradition reads: "The people disperse into exile."

sentences.zh: 二年二月，蘇州嘉興馬生角。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, in Jiaxing of Suzhou, a horse grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Zhonghe 2, a horse in Jiaxing, Suzhou, grew horns.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年夏四月，僖宗在鳳翔，馬尾皆咤蓬如篲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the second year of Guangqi, when Emperor Xizong was at Fengxiang, the tails of the horses all bristled erect like broom bristles.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in Guangqi 2, while Emperor Xizong was at Fengxiang, every horse's tail bristled upright like the splints of a broom.

sentences.zh: 咤，怒象。

translations.literal: Zha means the image of anger.
translations.idiomatic: "Zha" denotes an omen of wrath.

sentences.zh: 文德元年，李克用獻馬二，肘膝皆有鬣，長五寸許，蹄大如七寸甌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wende, Li Keyong presented two horses with mane on the elbows and knees, each about five cun long, and hooves as large as a seven-cun bowl.
translations.idiomatic: In Wende 1, Li Keyong presented two horses with mane growing on their elbows and knees, some five cun in length, and hooves as broad as a seven-cun bowl.

sentences.zh: 人痾武德四年，太原尼志覺死，十日而蘇。

translations.literal: Human deformity omens — In the fourth year of Wude, the nun Zhi Jue of Taiyuan died and revived after ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Human deformity omens. In Wude 4, the Taiyuan nun Zhi Jue died and came back to life ten days later.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十九年，衞州人劉道安頭生肉角，隱見不常，因以惑眾，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhenguan, Liu Dao'an of Weizhou grew a horn of flesh on his head, appearing and disappearing irregularly; he thereby deluded the multitude and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 19, Liu Dao'an of Weizhou grew a flesh horn on his head that flickered in and out of sight; he used it to mislead crowds and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 角，兵象；

translations.literal: Horns are the image of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Horns are an omen of war.

sentences.zh: 肉，不可以觸者。

translations.literal: Flesh cannot be touched.
translations.idiomatic: Flesh [as horn] is not something one may touch.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，淄州高苑民吳威妻、嘉州民辛道護妻皆一產四男。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui, the wife of the commoner Wu Wei of Gaoyuan in Zizhou and the wife of the commoner Xin Daohu of Jiazhou each gave birth to four sons in one delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 6, Wu Wei's wife of Gaoyuan in Zizhou and Xin Daohu's wife of Jiazhou each bore four sons in a single birth.

sentences.zh: 凡物反常則為妖，亦陰氣盛則母道壯也。

translations.literal: Whenever things depart from the norm they become demons; it is also that when yin qi flourishes, the way of the mother grows strong.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever creatures violate their proper form they become portents; it also means that when yin force grows overpowering, the maternal principle asserts itself.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，普州有人化為虎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, someone in Puzhou transformed into a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 3, a man in Puzhou transformed into a tiger.

sentences.zh: 虎，猛噬而不仁。

translations.literal: The tiger is fierce in tearing yet lacks benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger devours fiercely and knows no mercy.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳三年四月，涇州獻二小兒，連心異體。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Yifeng, Jingzhou presented two small children with joined hearts but separate bodies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yifeng 3, Jingzhou presented two infants joined at the chest but otherwise separate in body.

sentences.zh: 初，鶉觚縣衞士胡萬年妻吳生一男一女，其胸相連，餘各異體，乃析之，則皆死；

translations.literal: Earlier, Wu, wife of the garrison soldier Hu Wannian of Chiguo County, bore one boy and one girl whose chests were joined though the rest differed; they were separated, and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wu, wife of Hu Wannian, a guardsman of Chiguo County, had borne a boy and a girl joined at the chest while the rest of their bodies diverged; when surgeons separated them, both died.

sentences.zh: 又產，復然，俱男也，遂育之，至是四歲，以獻于朝。

translations.literal: She gave birth again, and it was the same, both males; they were then raised, and at this time they were four years old and were presented at court.
translations.idiomatic: She conceived again with the same outcome—again both boys—and this time they were reared; they were now four years old and were presented to the court.

sentences.zh: 永隆元年，長安獲女魃，長尺有二寸，其狀怪異。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonglong, a female drought demon was captured in Chang'an, one chi and two cun in height, of strange appearance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonglong 1, Chang'an officials seized a female drought demon a chi and two cun tall, of bizarre form.

sentences.zh: 詩曰：「旱魃為虐，如炎如焚。」

translations.literal: The Odes say: "The drought demon wreaks havoc, fierce as flame, fierce as fire."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "The drought demon wreaks havoc, blazing as flame, burning as fire."

sentences.zh: 是歲秋，不雨，至于明年正月。

translations.literal: That autumn it did not rain, continuing until the first month of the following year.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn brought no rain, and the drought lasted until the first month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年九月，萬年縣女子劉凝靜衣白衣，從者數人，升太史令廳，問比有何災異。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yonglong, Liu Ningjing, a woman of Wannian County, dressed in white and with several followers, ascended the hall of the Grand Astrologer and asked what calamities and anomalies had lately occurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yonglong 2, Liu Ningjing, a woman of Wannian County, clad in white and attended by several followers, entered the Grand Astrologer's hall and inquired what recent calamities and anomalies there had been.

sentences.zh: 令執之以聞。

translations.literal: The director detained her and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: The director had her seized and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 是夜，彗星見。

translations.literal: That night a comet appeared.
translations.idiomatic: That same night a comet appeared.

sentences.zh: 太史司天文、曆候，王者所以奉若天道、恭授民時者，非女子所當問。

translations.literal: The Grand Astrologer's office observes astronomy and the calendar and portents — what the ruler employs to align with the Way of Heaven and respectfully hand down the seasons to the people — and is not what women should inquire about.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Astrologer's office watches the heavens, calendrics, and omens on the ruler's behalf, so that he may align with heaven's way and grant the seasons to his people — work no woman should presume to question.

sentences.zh: 載初中，涪州民范端化為虎。

translations.literal: In the early Zaichu era, Fan Duan, a commoner of Fu Prefecture, transformed into a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zaichu era, Fan Duan, a commoner of Fu Prefecture, transformed into a tiger.

sentences.zh: 神功元年一月庚子，有人走入端門，又入則天門，至通天宮，閽及仗衞不之覺。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi of the first month of the first year of Shendgong, a man walked into the Duan Gate, then entered the Zetian Gate, reaching the Tongtian Palace; neither the gatekeepers nor the armed guards noticed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the first-month gengzi day of Shendgong 1, a man passed through the Duan Gate and then the Zetian Gate all the way to the Tongtian Palace, yet neither gate guards nor armed escorts perceived him.

sentences.zh: 時來俊臣婢產肉塊如二升器，剖之有赤蟲，須臾化為蜂，螫人而去。

translations.literal: At that time the maid of Lai Junchen gave birth to a lump of flesh like a two-sheng vessel; when cut open it contained red worms that in a moment transformed into bees, stung people, and flew away.
translations.idiomatic: About that time a maid of Lai Junchen bore a flesh mass the size of a two-sheng jar; when it was cut open, red worms inside instantly became bees that stung people and flew off.

sentences.zh: 久視二年正月，成州有大人跡見。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jiushi, giant footprints appeared in Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jiushi 2, giant human footprints were seen in Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 長安中，郴州佐史因病化為虎，欲食其嫂，擒之，乃人也，雖未全化，而虎毛生矣。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, a clerk of Chenzhou who fell ill transformed into a tiger and wished to devour his sister-in-law; when seized, he was still a man, though not wholly transformed, for tiger hair had already grown upon him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, a Chenzhou clerical aide who fell ill began turning into a tiger and tried to eat his sister-in-law; when seized he was still human, yet not fully so, for tiger hair had already sprouted on his body.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，狂人段萬謙潛入承天門，登太極殿，升御牀，自稱天子，且言：「我李安國也，人相我年三十二當為天子。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji, the madman Duan Wanqian stealthily entered the Chengtian Gate, ascended the Taiji Hall, climbed onto the imperial couch, declared himself Son of Heaven, and said: "I am Li Anguo; men have told me that at thirty-two I shall become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In Taiji 1, the madman Duan Wanqian slipped through the Chengtian Gate, mounted the Taiji Hall, climbed onto the imperial couch, proclaimed himself emperor, and declared: "I am Li Anguo; fortune-tellers say that at thirty-two I shall be emperor."

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年四月，冀州獻長人李家寵，八尺有五寸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, Jizhou presented the tall man Li Jiachong, eight chi and five cun in height.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiyuan 23, Jizhou presented the exceptionally tall Li Jiachong, measuring eight chi and five cun.

sentences.zh: 大曆十年二月，昭應婦人張產一男二女。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year of Dali, the woman Zhang of Zhaoying gave birth to one boy and two girls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Dali 10, Zhang, a woman of Zhaoying, bore one son and two daughters.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年正月丁亥，許州人李狗兒持仗上含元殿擊欄檻，伏誅。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai of the first month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan, Li Gou'er of Xuzhou, holding a weapon, ascended the Hanyuan Hall and struck the balustrade; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day of the first month in Zhenyuan 8, Li Gou'er of Xuzhou stormed the Hanyuan Hall armed and beat on the balustrade; he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 十年四月，恆州有巨人跡見。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the tenth year, giant footprints appeared in Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenyuan 10, giant footprints were seen in Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月戊申，狂人劉忠詣銀臺，稱白起令上表，天下有火災。

translations.literal: On the day wushen of the first month of the fifteenth year, the madman Liu Zhong went to the Yintai Gate, claiming that Bai Qi had ordered him to submit a memorial saying that fire disasters would engulf the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day of the first month in Zhenyuan 15, the madman Liu Zhong came to the Yintai Gate, declaring that Bai Qi had commanded him to submit a memorial warning of fire disasters across the land.

sentences.zh: 十七年十一月，翰林待詔戴少平死十有六日而蘇。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventeenth year, Dai Shaoping, a Hanlin awaiting edict, died and revived after sixteen days.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhenyuan 17, Dai Shaoping, a Hanlin Academician awaiting edicts, died and returned to life sixteen days later.

sentences.zh: 是歲，宣州南陵縣丞李嶷死，已殯三十日而蘇。

translations.literal: That year, Li Yao, assistant magistrate of Nanling in Xuanzhou, died and, after having been encoffined for thirty days, revived.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Li Yao, assistant magistrate of Nanling in Xuanzhou, died and came back to life thirty days after his interment.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，商州洪崖冶役夫將化為虎，眾以水沃之，不果化。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe, a smelting laborer at Hongya in Shangzhou was about to transform into a tiger; the crowd drenched him with water, and the transformation did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2, a smelter at Hongya in Shangzhou was on the verge of turning into a tiger; the workers poured water over him, and the transformation failed to complete.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年三月，民徐忠信潛入浴堂門。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Changqing, the commoner Xu Zhongxin secretly entered the bathhouse gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Changqing 4 (824), a commoner named Xu Zhongxin sneaked into the imperial bathhouse gate.

sentences.zh: 寶曆二年十二月，延州人賀文妻一產四男。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Baoli, He Wen's wife of Yanzhou gave birth to four boys at one delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Baoli 2 (826), He Wen's wife in Yanzhou gave birth to quadruplets—all boys.

sentences.zh: 大和二年十月，狂人劉德廣入含元殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Dahe, the madman Liu Deguang entered the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Dahe 2 (828), a madman named Liu Deguang entered the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 咸通七年，渭州有人生角寸許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xiantong, a man in Weizhou grew horns about a cun long.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 7 (866), a man in Weizhou grew horns roughly a cun in length.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下有兵。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "Under Heaven there will be armies."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication states: "War will spread across the realm."

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，太原晉陽民家有嬰兒，兩頭異頸，四手聯足。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, in a commoner's home at Jinyang, Taiyuan, there was an infant with two heads on a single neck and four hands joined at the feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Xiantong 13 (872), a commoner household at Jinyang in Taiyuan had an infant with two heads on one neck and four arms sharing joined feet.

sentences.zh: 此天下不一之妖。

translations.literal: This is a portent of the realm's lack of unity.
translations.idiomatic: This was a portent of a fractured realm.

sentences.zh: 是歲，民皇甫及年十四，暴長七尺餘，長啜大嚼，三倍如初，歲餘死。

translations.literal: That year, the commoner Huangfu Ji, age fourteen, suddenly grew to more than seven chi; he drank and chewed voraciously at three times his former rate, and died after more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: That same year a commoner named Huangfu Ji, fourteen years old, shot up to over seven chi; he drank and gorged at triple his usual appetite, then died a little more than a year later.

sentences.zh: 乾符六年秋，蜀郡婦人尹生子首如豕，目在脽下。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year of Qianfu, a woman of Shu commandery named Yin gave birth to a child whose head was like a pig's, with eyes below the buttocks.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Qianfu 6 (879), a woman surnamed Yin in Shu commandery bore a child with a piglike head and eyes set beneath the rump.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「君失道。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The ruler has lost the Way."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication states: "The ruler has lost the Way."

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，隰州溫泉民家有死者，既葬且半月，行人聞聲呼地下，其家發之，則復生，歲餘乃死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, in a commoner's family at Wenquan in Xizhou there was one who had died; after burial, and half a month had passed, passersby heard a voice calling from underground; the family exhumed him, and he revived; after more than a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangqi 1 (885), in a household at Wenquan in Xizhou a man had died and been buried; half a month later travelers heard someone calling from beneath the ground; when the family opened the grave he revived, only to die again a year or so later.

sentences.zh: 二年春，鳳翔郿縣女子未齓化為丈夫，旬日而死。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year, at Meixian in Fengxiang a girl before her teeth had shed transformed into a man, and died after ten days.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Guangqi 2 (886), a girl in Meixian, Fengxiang, who had not yet shed her baby teeth turned into a man and died ten days later.

sentences.zh: 京房易傳曰：「茲謂陰昌，賊人為王。」

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "This is called yin flourishing; a thief will become king."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Book of Changes says: "This is yin run riot; brigands will make themselves kings."

sentences.zh: 大順元年六月，資州兵王全義妻如孕，覺物漸下入股，至足大拇，痛甚，坼而生珠如彈丸，漸長大如杯。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Dashun, the wife of Wang Quanyi, a soldier of Zizhou, seemed pregnant; she felt something gradually descending into the thigh, to the big toe of the foot; the pain was severe; it split open and a pearl was born like a pellet, gradually growing as large as a cup.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Dashun 1 (890), the wife of Zizhou soldier Wang Quanyi seemed pregnant; she felt something work downward into her thigh and down to her big toe, with agonizing pain; her flesh split open and disgorged a pearl the size of a pellet that slowly swelled to the size of a cup.

sentences.zh: 天祐二年五月，潁州汝陰民彭文妻一產三男。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Tianyou, Peng Wen's wife of Ruyin, Yingzhou, gave birth to three boys at one delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianyou 2 (905), Peng Wen's wife in Ruyin, Yingzhou, gave birth to triplets—all boys.

sentences.zh: 疫貞觀十年，關內、河東大疫。

translations.literal: Plague — In the tenth year of Zhenguan, great plague within Guannei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Plague. In Zhenguan 10 (636), Guannei and Hedong suffered a great epidemic.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，澤州疫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year, plague at Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhenguan 15 (641), Ze Prefecture was stricken with plague.

sentences.zh: 十六年夏，穀、涇、徐、戴、虢五州疫。

translations.literal: In summer of the sixteenth year, plague in the five prefectures of Gu, Jing, Xu, Dai, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenguan 16 (642), plague struck Gu, Jing, Xu, Dai, and Guo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十七年夏，潭、濠、廬三州疫。

translations.literal: In summer of the seventeenth year, plague in the three prefectures of Tan, Hao, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenguan 17 (643), Tan, Hao, and Lu prefectures were stricken.

sentences.zh: 十八年，廬、濠、巴、普、郴五州疫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, plague in the five prefectures of Lu, Hao, Ba, Pu, and Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 18 (644), Lu, Hao, Ba, Pu, and Chen prefectures suffered plague.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卿州大疫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, great plague at Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 22 (648), Qing Prefecture suffered a great epidemic.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年三月，楚州大疫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year of Yonghui, great plague at Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yonghui 6 (655), Chuzhou suffered a great plague.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年冬，大疫，兩京死者相枕於路。

translations.literal: In winter of the first year of Yongchun, a great plague; in the two capitals the dead lay pillow to pillow along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Yongchun 1 (682), a great epidemic swept the land; in the two capitals the dead lay heaped along the roads.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「國將有恤，則邪亂之氣先被于民，故疫。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "When the state is about to suffer mourning, evil and chaotic qi first reach the common people—hence plague."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication states: "When the realm is headed for catastrophe, malign and rebellious forces strike the people first—hence epidemic plague."

sentences.zh: 景龍元年夏，自京師至山東、河北疫，死者千數。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Jinglong, plague from the capital to Shandong and Hebei; the dead numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Jinglong 1 (707), plague spread from the capital to Shandong and Hebei, killing thousands.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，江東大疫，死者過半。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, great plague in Jiangdong; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 (762), Jiangdong suffered a great epidemic; more than half the people died.

sentences.zh: 貞元六年夏，淮南、浙西、福建道疫。

translations.literal: In summer of the sixth year of Zhenyuan, plague in the circuits of Huainan, Zhexi, and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenyuan 6 (790), plague ravaged Huainan, Zhexi, and Fujian circuits.

sentences.zh: 元和元年夏，浙東大疫，死者太半。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Yuanhe, great plague in Zhedong; more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Yuanhe 1 (806), Zhedong suffered a great plague; well over half the people died.

sentences.zh: 大和六年春，自劍南至浙西大疫。

translations.literal: In spring of the sixth year of Dahe, great plague from Jiannan to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Dahe 6 (832), a great epidemic ran from Jiannan to Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 開成五年夏，福、建、台、明四州疫。

translations.literal: In summer of the fifth year of Kaicheng, plague in the four prefectures of Fu, Jian, Tai, and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kaicheng 5 (840), Fu, Jian, Tai, and Ming prefectures were stricken.

sentences.zh: 咸通十年，宣、歙、兩浙疫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xiantong, plague in Xuan, She, and the two Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiantong 10 (869), plague struck Xuanzhou, Shezhou, and both Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 大順二年春，淮南疫，死者十三四。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Dashun, plague in Huainan; three or four of every ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Dashun 2 (891), Huainan was ravaged by plague; three or four out of every ten died.

sentences.zh: 天鳴天寶十四載五月，天鳴，聲若雷。

translations.literal: Heaven's cry — In the fifth month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, heaven cried with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's cry. In the fifth month of Tianbao 14 (755), a heaven's cry sounded like thunder.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「人君有憂。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "The ruler has cares."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication states: "The sovereign will face grief."

sentences.zh: 貞元二十一年八月，天鳴，在西北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-first year of Zhenyuan, heaven cried in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhenyuan 21 (805), a heaven's cry was heard in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 中和三年三月，浙西天鳴，聲如轉磨。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Zhonghe, heaven cried in western Zhe; the sound was like turning a millstone.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhonghe 3 (883), western Zhe heard a heaven's cry like a millstone grinding.

sentences.zh: 無雲而雨元和十二年正月乙酉，星見而雨。

translations.literal: Rain without clouds — On yiyou in the first month of the twelfth year of Yuanhe, stars appeared and it rained.
translations.idiomatic: Rain without clouds. On the yiyou day of the first month in Yuanhe 12 (817), stars showed forth and rain fell.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「無雲而雨，是謂天泣。」

translations.literal: Prognostication states: "When it rains without clouds, this is called heaven weeping."
translations.idiomatic: The prognostication states: "Rain without cloud cover is called heaven weeping."

sentences.zh: 隕石永徽四年八月己亥，隕石于同州馮翊十八，光耀，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Meteorites — On jihai in the eighth month of the fourth year of Yonghui, meteorites fell at eighteen places in Fengyi of Tongzhou, shining brightly, with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Meteorites. On the jihai day of the eighth month in Yonghui 4 (653), meteorites fell in eighteen locations at Fengyi in Tongzhou, blazing bright, with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 近星隕而化也。

translations.literal: These are falling stars that have transformed.
translations.idiomatic: They are shooting stars that have transmuted as they fall.

sentences.zh: 庶民惟星，自上而隕，民去其上之象。

translations.literal: The common people are stars; when stars fall from above, it is the image of the people casting off their superiors.
translations.idiomatic: The common folk are likened to stars; a fall from on high images the people deserting their superiors.

sentences.zh: 一曰：「人君為詐妄所蔽則然。」

translations.literal: One account states: "When the ruler is veiled by fraud and presumption, this results."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading states: "This happens when the sovereign is blinded by deceit and falsehood."
